read.bigIdea: Blue agave, cooked, crushed and distilled.
read.where: Tequila is made in Mexico from **blue Weber agave**. The heart of the plant, the **piña**, is cooked to turn its starch into sugar, crushed, fermented and distilled. Cooking in ovens keeps the flavor bright and peppery; there’s no pit smoke as in many mezcals.

keyPoints.line: tells you: look for “100% de agave.”

read.bigIdea: Read the label: 100% agave or just “tequila.”
read.where: **100% de agave** tequila is made only from agave sugars and must be bottled in its production region. A tequila that just says **“tequila”** (often called **mixto**) needs only **51%** of its sugars from agave; the rest can come from other sugars.
read.mixup: **100% agave** says so on the label. If it doesn’t, it’s a **mixto**.

keyPoints.line: is unaged or rested under two months.
rests at least two months in oak.
ages at least one year; extra añejo, three.

read.bigIdea: Five classes, from unaged to three years.
read.where: **Blanco** is unaged or rested under two months. **Joven** is usually blanco with color or a little aged tequila mixed in. **Reposado** rests in oak at least **two months**. **Añejo** ages at least **one year** in oak of 600 liters or less. **Extra añejo** ages at least **three years**. **Cristalino** is aged tequila filtered clear; it isn’t its own legal class.

keyPoints.line: is the most common agave; tobalá is wild.
from roasting agave in earthen pits.
mezcal is distilled in clay pots.

read.bigIdea: Any of many agaves, often roasted in pits.
read.where: **Mezcal** is an agave spirit made mostly in **Oaxaca**, from many kinds of agave. **Espadín** is the most common; **tobalá** is a smaller, wild agave; an **ensamble** blends several. Roasting the agave in **earthen pits** gives the smoky taste. The label says how it’s made: **mezcal**, **mezcal artesanal** (pit ovens, traditional crushing) or **mezcal ancestral** (pit ovens, hand crushing, clay pot stills).
read.mixup: All tequila is a kind of agave spirit, but **tequila** must be blue Weber agave from its own region. **Mezcal** can use many agaves.

keyPoints.line: is tequila, lime and orange liqueur.
is tequila, grapefruit soda and lime.

read.bigIdea: From the Margarita to the Oaxaca Old Fashioned.
read.where: The **Margarita** is tequila, lime and orange liqueur. The **Paloma** is tequila with grapefruit soda and lime. The **Oaxaca Old Fashioned** uses tequila **and** mezcal. The **Naked and Famous** is mezcal, Aperol, yellow Chartreuse and lime. **Blanco** keeps citrus drinks bright; **reposado** and **añejo** suit stirred drinks.

sources: Mexican mezcal standard NOM-070-SCFI-2016 (as summarized on Wikipedia); Mexican tequila standard NOM-006-SCFI (as summarized by Difford’s Guide); Our book: the classic and house cocktail specs in this app. Checked Nov 8, 2026.
